headline: The front end blinked and the long end didn't: 2s10s steepened 5bp to 37bp while Brent fell 8.1% — the bond market is now pricing cuts and term premium at the same time.
summary: The rates shock changed shape today. Bills and 2s finally gave ground — 3-month down 3bp to 4.25%, 2-year down 3bp to 4.89% — while 10s rose 2bp to 5.26% and 30s rose 3bp to 5.59%, both still pinned at the 100th percentile of the last year. That is bear steepening: 2s10s +5bp to 0.37, 3m10y +5bp to 1.01 and at the top of its range. The 10-year real yield sits at 2.91%, +49bp on the month, 37% above its 200-day, acceleration 1.42, while 5y and 10y breakevens are inert at 2.34% and 2.35%. Nothing about this is inflation; it is term premium. And the volatility leg keeps compounding: MOVE +4.7% to 106.6, +50.2% on the month, z=2.76, acceleration 1.93. TLT (78.23), IEF and LQD all sit at the 0th percentile of their 52-week range. Rates composite stuck at -85; risk regime deteriorated to -19 from -15.

Energy cracked hard enough to change the inflation math. Brent -8.1% to 96.76, WTI -3.0% to 89.82, RBOB -6.2% and now -10.3% on the month with z=-1.05. Breakevens did not move on it, which tells you crude is trading its own supply story, not demand collapse — copper was up 1.2% and copper/gold sits at the 97th percentile with acceleration 1.61, growth pulse +16. The pain was in the levered end of energy: OIH -2.4%, -9.1% on the month, relative strength -8.7% and below its 200-day, while XOM (+3.0% 1m) and CVX (+1.2%) barely flinched. Precious metals put in a second day of repair after last week's flush: gold +0.8% to 4,202, GDX +1.3%, GDXJ +1.5%, NEM +0.9%, against acceleration z-scores of -3.2, -2.9 and -3.18. Capitulation prints like that rarely need a third test.

Inside equities the index is still lying about the tape. SPX -0.2% to 7,670.8, 6.3% above its 200-day at the 91st percentile; NDX +0.2%, QQQ/SPY +0.4% with z=1.36. Leadership is two blocks wide: semis (SMH +1.1%, +9.7% on the month; SOXX +1.2%, +11.6%; ASML +3.6%, TSM +0.9%, MU +1.1%, AMD +30.5% on the month) and META, up 3.2% today and 27.9% on the month with z=2.24 and acceleration 1.85. Even ORCL bounced 3.9% off a -28.6% year. Underneath, breadth made no repair: RSP/SPY z=-2.02 at the 10th percentile, IWM/SPY -5.0% on the month, IYT/SPY at the 6th percentile, DJT -8.1% and DJI -4.1% on the month. The new damage is financials. The curve steepened and banks still fell — KRE -1.0%, KBE -1.0%, XLF -6.7% on the month with relative strength -6.3%, GS -11.0%, IAI -8.6%, BX -19.9% with z=-2.05 and acceleration -1.9. That is not net interest margin; that is capital markets and private credit marks.

The dollar is still the squeeze channel and credit still hasn't paid. DXY 101.37 with acceleration 1.06, USDCHF at a fresh 52-week high, USDCAD +2.4% on the month with acceleration 1.60, and USDMXN the standout: +0.6% today, +4.6% on the week, +6.1% on the month, z=2.37, acceleration 1.96. EM equity in dollars reflects it — TUR -15.0% on the month, EZA -8.3%, KSA -7.3%, EWW -5.8%, INDA -5.3% — while AUDJPY is -4.6% with z=-1.82. Meanwhile HYG is only -0.2% but with z=-1.57 and acceleration -1.32, and HYG/IEF still sits at the 94th percentile. Spreads have absorbed none of what duration already has. And the hedge is cheap: VIX 16.04 at the 15th percentile, VIX3M at the 6th, SKEW -3.5% on the month, but VIX/VIX3M turned up to 0.887 with acceleration 1.50. The power-and-hard-asset complex, last quarter's crowded long, is in outright liquidation: NLR -11.8% on the month at the 2nd percentile (acceleration -2.35), URA -12.1%, REMX -16.3%, XME -12.4% with acceleration -2.39, TAN -10.7%.

good.text: The front end finally eased: 3-month -3bp to 4.25%, 2-year -3bp to 4.89%, and both curve measures steepened (2s10s +5bp to 0.37, 3m10y +5bp to 1.01, top of its 52-week range). The first piece of policy relief in weeks.

Crude crack is a consumer tax cut: Brent -8.1% to 96.76, WTI -3.0% to 89.82, RBOB -6.2% and -10.3% on the month — with 5y and 10y breakevens unchanged at 2.34% and 2.35%, so no inflation impulse lost or gained.

Precious metals washout looks finished: gold +0.8% to 4,202, GDX +1.3%, GDXJ +1.5%, NEM +0.9% — a second up day after acceleration z-scores of -3.2, -2.9 and -3.18, which is textbook capitulation exhaustion.
AI hardware leadership is not fading: SMH +1.1% (+9.7% 1m), SOXX +1.2% (+11.6%), ASML +3.6%, TSM +0.9%, MU +1.1%, AMD +30.5% on the month; SMH/SPY z=1.34 at the 74th percentile.
Megacap repair broadened at the top: META +3.2% and +27.9% on the month (z=2.24, acceleration 1.85), ORCL +3.9% off a -28.6% year, QQQ/SPY +0.4% with z=1.36.

Growth-sensitive metals and crypto are quietly firm: copper +1.2%, copper/gold at the 97th percentile (z=1.32, acceleration 1.61), SOL +15.7% and MSTR +21.5% on the month, BTC +38.9% over three months.

bad.text: Long-end selling continues even as the front end rallies: 10y +2bp to 5.26%, 30y +3bp to 5.59%, both 100th percentile; the 10-year real yield is 2.91%, +49bp on the month, 37% above its 200-day with acceleration 1.42. Term premium, not growth.

Bond volatility is still accelerating the wrong way: MOVE +4.7% to 106.6, +50.2% on the month, z=2.76, acceleration 1.93. TLT, IEF and LQD all sit at the 0th percentile of their 52-week range. Collateral is repricing faster than equities.

Financials broke despite a steeper curve — the tell that this is credit, not margin: BX -19.9% on the month (z=-2.05, acceleration -1.9), GS -11.0%, IAI -8.6%, KBE and KRE both -1.0% today, XLF relative strength -6.3%.

Breadth made no repair at cycle lows: RSP/SPY z=-2.02 at the 10th percentile, IWM/SPY -5.0% on the month, IYT/SPY at the 6th, DJT -8.1% and DJI -4.1% on the month while SPX sits 6.3% above its 200-day.

Credit is rolling without being priced: HYG -0.2% but z=-1.57 with acceleration -1.32, LQD -3.3% on the month — yet HYG/IEF still sits at the 94th percentile. VIX at 16.04 (15th percentile) with VIX/VIX3M turning up to 0.887, acceleration 1.50.

The power/hard-asset trade is in liquidation: NLR -11.8% on the month at the 2nd percentile (acceleration -2.35), URA -12.1%, REMX -16.3%, XME -12.4% (acceleration -2.39), COPX -9.5%, TAN -10.7%. The dollar squeeze compounds it — USDMXN z=2.37, TUR -15.0%, EWW -5.8%.

trades.name: Long-end Treasuries (TLT)
trades.line: Short TLT: front end prices cuts, long end prices term premium
trades.expr: Short TLT outright or buy the Dec 76/70 put spread; funded version is short 30y futures vs long 2y futures for a 2s30s steepener.
trades.thesis: The curve is re-steepening from the wrong end. The market is starting to price easing (3m -3bp, 2y -3bp) while the 30-year sells off to 5.59% and the 10-year real yield hits 2.91%, +49bp in a month. Cuts into a 2.35% breakeven and a 100th-percentile long end means more term premium, not less.
trades.trigger: Today's 5bp steepening in both 2s10s (to 0.37) and 3m10y (to 1.01) alongside a 30y up 3bp, with MOVE +4.7% to 106.6 (z=2.76, acc 1.93) and TLT at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.stop: TLT closes back above 81 or 10y back under 5.05% with MOVE below 95 — that would say the long end is accepting the cut narrative.

trades.name: Long QQQ / short IWM
trades.line: Long QQQ vs short IWM: breadth at cycle lows, 2y still 4.89%
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long QQQ versus short IWM, rebalanced weekly; cheaper via long QQQ Dec calls vs short IWM Dec calls.
trades.thesis: Leadership is two blocks wide and getting narrower, not broader. Cash-rich AI hardware compounders don't care about a 5.26% 10-year; leveraged small caps and regional-bank-adjacent domestics do. Every attempt at broadening this quarter has failed inside a week.
trades.trigger: QQQ/SPY z=1.36 and SMH/SPY z=1.34 versus RSP/SPY z=-2.02 at the 10th percentile and IWM/SPY -5.0% on the month; RUT -5.5% and MDY -4.2% on the month while NDX is +3.1%.
trades.stop: RSP/SPY reclaims its 200-day (3.9% above spot) or SMH/SPY falls 5% from here — that is a leadership change, exit.

trades.name: Blackstone (BX)
trades.line: Short BX: -20% in a month and credit hasn't paid yet
trades.expr: Short BX stock, or buy the January 110/90 put spread; broaden with a smaller short in IAI.
trades.thesis: Private-credit and capital-markets marks are the last thing to reprice in a duration shock. BX is telling you it has started: -19.9% on the month with z=-2.05 and acceleration -1.9, at the 20th percentile of its range, while HYG/IEF still sits at the 94th percentile pretending spreads are fine.
trades.trigger: BX -0.5% today on top of -8.1% on the week; IAI -8.6% and GS -11.0% on the month with the curve steepening — that combination is credit, not net interest margin. HYG z=-1.57 with acceleration -1.32.
trades.stop: BX reclaims 128, or HYG makes a new 3-month high above 79 with HYG/IEF still rising — spreads refusing to widen kills the thesis.

trades.name: Gold miners (GDX)
trades.line: Long GDX: -3.2 sigma washout, gold stabilizing two days
trades.expr: Buy GDX spot, or the November 90/105 call spread; add GDXJ for higher beta on a 1:3 sizing.
trades.thesis: The complex was liquidated, not de-rated. GDX fell 10.6% in a month with an acceleration z-score of -3.2 and GDX/GOLD acceleration of -3.01 — forced-seller prints. Gold at 4,202 is still +9.0% year-on-year with real yields as the only headwind, and a steepening curve with cuts priced at the front end is the setup gold likes.
trades.trigger: Second consecutive up day: gold +0.8%, GDX +1.3%, GDXJ +1.5%, NEM +0.9%, after gold's -7.2% month. Gold/silver turning up (68.42) means the flush hit the levered leg hardest.
trades.stop: Gold closes below 4,050 or GDX below 82 — that reopens the liquidation.

trades.name: Short OIH / long XLE
trades.line: Short OIH vs long XLE: Brent -8% hits services, not majors
trades.expr: Short OIH against a long in XLE, dollar-neutral; substitute XOM/CVX for XLE if you want less refining beta.
trades.thesis: An 8% one-day break in Brent kills the marginal capex dollar long before it dents integrated cash flow. Services carry the operating leverage; majors carry the dividend and the buyback. The spread has already started and has room.
trades.trigger: Brent -8.1% to 96.76 and WTI -3.0% today, RBOB -10.3% on the month; OIH -2.4% today, -9.1% on the month, relative strength -8.7% and below its 200-day, while XLE is only -1.2% on the month and XOM is +3.0%.
trades.stop: Brent back above 104, or OIH above 400 — a supply-driven spike re-rates capex expectations.
trades.target: OIH 340 with XLE flat; roughly 10% on the pair.

trades.name: USD/MXN
trades.line: Long USD/MXN: carry unwind, z=2.4 and accelerating
trades.expr: Long USD/MXN spot or 3-month forwards; equity proxy is a short in EWW.
trades.thesis: The highest-carry, most crowded EM long is unwinding into a 4.89% 2-year US yield and a dollar that is grinding higher on every cross. This is the one place the squeeze has not paused, and positioning unwinds of this type run further than the first 6%.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +0.6% today, +4.6% on the week, +6.1% on the month with z=2.37 and acceleration 1.96 — the highest acceleration in the FX block. Confirmed by CEW -1.5%, AUDJPY -4.6% on the month (z=-1.82) and USDCHF at a 52-week high.
trades.stop: 17.55 — a close below the pre-squeeze level means the carry bid is back.

trades.name: SPX downside convexity
trades.line: Buy SPX put spread: VIX 16 vs 10th-pctile breadth
trades.expr: Buy the November SPX 7,300/6,900 put spread (roughly 5% out of the money), financed partly by selling a 5% OTM call if you are already long index.
trades.thesis: You are being offered index insurance at 16 vol while the internals of that index are at cycle lows and bond vol is at a 2.8 sigma high. The gap between an index 6.3% above its 200-day and breadth at the 10th percentile closes one of two ways, and only one of them is cheap to own.
trades.trigger: VIX 16.04 at the 15th percentile and VIX3M at the 6th, SKEW -3.5% on the month — but VIX/VIX3M turned up to 0.887 with acceleration 1.50 while RSP/SPY z=-2.02 and HYG accelerates lower at -1.32.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M back below 0.85 with RSP/SPY turning up and MOVE under 95 — then the vol bid is genuinely gone; cut the premium.
trades.target: SPX 7,250 / VIX into the mid-20s; take profit at a 3x on the spread.
